general_notes: Most candidates fall into five kinds: (1) the exact painting inset in a flat border frame; (2) a full-composition in-app version on a dark round vignette, slightly smaller and softer; (3) a tightly zoomed in-app crop that cuts off the legs and feet; (4) a heavily blurred copy of the painting; (5) a different 3D CG character. Within each state the in-app versions were often impossible for me to tell apart (idle A/B/C/H; fierce B/F/H). Where I saw differences, they were in ember density (joyful C sparse, F densest; fierce G richer) or smoke (depleted H thinner), and those judgements are uncertain at this resolution. All animation loops are very low amplitude: the character is essentially a still image with flame and ember flicker, so identity stability is high but the expressiveness of the motion is limited. The depleted target itself has a grey rectangle at bottom right, which the framed candidate F keeps and the vignette versions hide; I did not penalise its absence. I judged motion from six sampled frames only, so smoothness between frames and loop seams could not be checked.
